title: Grayscale on the CPU
author: Dimitris Yfantidis
summary: The same filter as a single-threaded C loop, for comparison.
description: Converts the same 15,000-pixel-wide photo to grayscale with a plain C loop on one CPU core, prints how long it took and shows the result. Run the GPU version too and compare the times.
how_it_works: Two nested loops walk the image row by row and pixel by pixel, replacing red, green and blue with the pixel's luminance and keeping alpha.
This version computes luminance in integer arithmetic with the older Rec. 601 weights, (299 R + 587 G + 114 B) / 1000, so its grays differ very slightly from the GPU version's Rec. 709 ones.
highlights: The time in the console (the terminal button at the top): one core visits every pixel in turn.
The image looks the same as the GPU result; the difference is in how long it took.
